newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND HAS NO OBJECTION TO PAINTMAKERS' MERGER.
newsitem.headline: POLAND HAS NO OBJECTION TO PAINTMAKERS' MERGER.

text.p: Poland's anti-monopoly office has no objection to the planned merger between paintmakers Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw , Polifarb Cieszyn said in a statement on Friday.
The two firms plan to merge at mid-year, a move which must first be approved by shareholders.
Under the plan Cieszyn would raise its share capital by 2,978,820 shares to equal Wroclaw's 22,103,820 shares.
Later Cieszyn would set another issue for Wroclaw shareholders and a one-for-one share exchange would take place to effect the merger.
Wroclaw's deputy president told Reuters last month that because both companies were similar in size and market capitalisation shareholders of neither firm would lose out on the deal.
He said the new entity would be able to produce at both Wroclaw and Cieszyn with the city of Wroclaw chosen as the headquarters of the new firm.
Analysts estimate that the two firms together command about 40 percent of Poland's paint market but expect them to come under increased pressure from international competitors.
According to preliminary figures Cieszyn made a net profit of 19.1 million zlotys last year on sales of 306.5 million.
Wroclaw made a net profit of 18.6 million zlotys on sales of 204.9 million zlotys. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
